subject: Renewal: phased fractional buckets + billing-cycle smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Asha Menon <asha@cardinalai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity growth + renewal timing

Hi Monica,

Quick note — Cardinal AI is planning to onboard an additional product line in August which will materially increase token consumption. We expect a ~45% uplift starting 2026-08-01 and would like to: (a) increase committed capacity mid-contract, and (b) align the renewal to 2027-02-01 so all seats co-term.

Primary asks:
- A practical mid-contract uplift path that doesn't force us into an immediate annual prepay.
- Any ability to smooth billing across invoicing cycles to avoid a single large spike this quarter.
- A discount framework for committed incremental volume (we're sensitive to price steps).

I've attached a short usage export so you can see baseline consumption. Open to a quick call this week.

Thanks,
Asha
Head of Platform
Cardinal AI

Attachment: usage_report_Q1.csv (CSV, 78 KB)
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha@cardinalai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity growth + renewal timing

Hi Asha — thanks for the heads up and the export, that helps. We can definitely support a mid-contract uplift without forcing an annual prepay. High-level options I propose below; happy to walk through on a call.

Option A — Phased fractional buckets (recommended):
- Add incremental committed buckets in 3 fractions (25% / 15% / final remainder) over 3 billing periods.
- Each fractional bucket is priced at a mild uplift discount vs on-demand (e.g., 8% discount on the incremental bucket).
- At your chosen co-term date (2027-02-01) we roll the total committed amount into a single co-term contract and give a blended pricing floor.

Option B — Accelerator voucher + true-up:
- Provide a one-time accelerator voucher to cap short-term overage for 60 days while we migrate traffic.
- True-up to committed levels at co-term with a conversion credit for the voucher value.

Billing smoothing notes:
- We can invoice the incremental commitment across the quarter in equal installments (monthly) so you don't receive a lump-sum for the uplift month.
- Alternatively, split the uplift charge across the following two invoices to match your cashflow.

Ben and Vivek — can you confirm feasibility for the fractional-bucket billing and what the discount bands look like for incremental commitments?

If this works, I'll formalize the proposal and attach a short amendment draft. Call? Wed 11:00 AM PT works for me.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0147

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity growth + renewal timing

Monica — high level OK from pricing. A few practical constraints and suggested bands: 
- Fractional buckets are operationally doable; we treat them as separate committed lines and reconcile at co-term.
- Discount bands for incremental committed volume (increment = new committed - existing committed):
  * 0-20% incremental: 5% incremental discount
  * 20-50% incremental: 10% incremental discount
  * 50%+ incremental: 15% incremental discount (requires CSM + executive sponsor approval)
- For mid-contract annualization to co-term we can offer a pro-rata conversion with a 3% blended-rate credit applied to the newly annualized portion if Cardinal commits to a 12-month post-rollout term.

Note: the 15% band needs approval due to margin impact; flagging for leadership. Also, document the voucher as a non-refundable credit applied against the first two invoices after uplift.

Ben
VP Sales Operations

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha@cardinalai.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity growth + renewal timing

Asha / Monica — logistics from billing side:
- We can implement monthly amortization for the uplift across the next 3 invoices to smooth the spike. That requires an amendment specifying uplift start date and the amortization window.
- If Cardinal prefers equal installments over 6 months, we can do that too; we'd model the cashflow impact in the attached amendment.
- Voucher handling: we'll issue a voucher line item (non-refundable credit) that applies to overage charges for 60 days; any unused voucher value converts into a one-time invoice credit at co-term.

I've drafted a short amendment template and attached it to this thread (Cardinal_proposal_v2.pdf). Monica — if you want, drop the values from Ben's bands into the draft and I'll run it through finance approval queue.

– Vivek
Director, Billing & Revenue Ops

Attachment: Cardinal_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Asha Menon <asha@cardinalai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity growth + renewal timing

Thanks all — this looks reasonable and pragmatic. A couple quick asks before we sign: 
1) Can we lock the 10% band for the expected uplift (we believe we'll be ~40% incremental once rollout completes)?
2) We'd prefer the 6-month equal installment smoothing to keep Q3 budgeting tidy.
3) Please confirm that the voucher will cover overages during the migration window and that any remaining voucher converts to credit at co-term.

If you can update the amendment to reflect the 10% band for the expected uplift and the 6-month amortization, we can route internally for approval and sign via DocuSign. Wed morning signature target on our side.

Best,
Asha
Head of Platform
Cardinal AI
